thesis: Remitly Global (Nasdaq: RELY), digital remittances. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-04) and Ex 99.1 read. Q3 revenue 509.8M vs 419.5M (+22%), 9M revenue 1,457.8M vs 1,193.0M (+22%); send volume Q3 24.4B (+25%), 9M 70.0B (+29%); active customers 10.34M vs 8.86M (+17%); 9M income from operations 189.8M vs 38.7M; 9M net income 322.5M vs 26.7M but includes a 136.0M tax benefit from releasing the US deferred tax valuation allowance (9M pre-tax income 186.5M; at an assumed 21% rate normalized 9M NI would be about 147M, own estimate). Guidance (Ex 99.1): FY2026 revenue 1.989 to 1.991B (+22%), Adjusted EBITDA 441 to 443M; Q4 revenue 531 to 533M (+20% to +21%), Adjusted EBITDA 104 to 106M (non-GAAP, not reconciled by the company). TTM NI (USD M) = FY2025 67.9 + 9M26 322.5 - 9M25 26.7 = 363.7. Close 20.06 (2026-11-19) x 214,012,570 shares (10-Q cover, 2026-11-02) = 4.29B = 11.8x TTM NI (inflated by the one time tax benefit; normalized, about 22x annualized 9M at an assumed 21% tax rate: own rough arithmetic, not a TTM figure). 9M FCF (OCF 309.5 less PP&E 8.5 less capitalized software 10.4) = 290.6M = 6.8% of market cap (9M, not annualized); after 9M SBC 101.7M = 189.0M (4.4%). TTM FCF is not computed: 2025 cash flow was reclassified (customer funds moved from operating to financing, 49.7M in 9M25) so the FY2025 10-K OCF 325.1M is on an older basis. Balance sheet 2026-09-30: cash 669.1M, disbursement prefunding 287.4M, customer funds receivable 357.1M, customer liabilities 213.3M, debt 2.9M short term and none long term (155M repaid), revolver upsized to 1.0B on 2026-10-26 (10-30 8-K), total liabilities 426.9M, equity 1,226.4M. Buyback: 4.5M shares for 80.0M in 9M, authorization raised to 500M (96.1M left at 9-30 before the raise). Possible market view: remittance is a low moat, price competitive, immigration policy sensitive business and the earnings jump is accounting. Differing evidence: 29% volume growth, customers +17%, operating margin 13.0% in 9M vs 3.2%, essentially no debt, buyback. Stock fell about 8% in the four sessions to 11-19 (21.93 on 11-16 to 20.06; cause not investigated). What could close the gap: continued 20% growth with rising GAAP operating margin.
counterthesis: Remittances are exposed to US immigration enforcement, remittance taxes and corridor concentration (India, Mexico, Philippines); marketing 294.7M in 9M (20% of revenue) is the growth engine and customer acquisition cost can rise. Competitors (Wise, Western Union, Intermex, banks, stablecoin rails) can compress take rates; revenue grows slower than send volume (+22% vs +29% in 9M), implying a falling take rate. SBC 101.7M is 7% of 9M revenue and diluted shares are 220.5M vs 214.0M outstanding. The headline net income is flattered by a 136M valuation allowance release. Customer funds and prefunding (about 644M of receivables and prefunding versus 213M customer liabilities) depend on revolver and bank partners; operational or regulatory problems with money transmission licenses could be severe. Adjusted EBITDA guidance is non-GAAP and unreconciled. Peers and history not compared; legal and risk factors not read.
invalidation: Invalidated if send volume growth slows below about 15% while marketing stays near 20% of revenue, if take rate compression outpaces operating leverage, if regulatory action or a remittance tax materially cuts volume, or if GAAP operating income falls back toward 2025 levels.
